programme.title: Lost Worlds of South America
programme.sub-title: Chavín and the Rise of Religious Authority
programme.desc: How the site of Chavin marks the emergence of religion as the focus of public art; Chavin's architecture, with images of its characteristic fanged deity; later religious iconography and artifacts suggesting that Chavin was the center of a cult.

programme.title: Lost Worlds of South America
programme.sub-title: Cupisnique to Salinar - Elite Rulers and War
programme.desc: The waning of Chavin's culture; new elements in the Chavin region's archeological record; encountering the Salinar culture; a settlement pattern showing no ceremonial architecture; the first elite housing; evidence of defensive citadels.

programme.title: The Mongol Empire
programme.sub-title: The Mongols' Place in World History
programme.desc: Starting with eyewitness accounts of the arrival of the Mongol armies at unsuspecting cities across Eurasia, Professor Benjamin launches his survey of the Mongol Empire; he sketches the history of civilizations destined to be ruled by the Mongols.

programme.title: The Mongol Empire
programme.sub-title: The Origins of Eurasian Steppe Nomadism
programme.desc: Using a big history angle to understand the origin of militarized nomadism in the pastoral culture that develops on the grasslands of Eurasia; the paradox of nomadic empires that rarely build cities, yet still interact with the great civilizations.

programme.title: The Mongol Empire
programme.desc: Learning about the one who establishes the Mongol Empire in the 13th century, Chinggis Khan; previous Mongolian-centered empires establish a template that is perfected by Chinggis; tracing the precursors to Turkic rulers in the 7th and 8th centuries.

programme.title: The Mongol Empire
programme.desc: Drawing on "The Secret History of the Mongols", charting the rise of a minor Mongol chief's obscure son who earns the title of the universal ruler; his martial daring and hairbreadth escapes have all the drama of a Hollywood epic; Borte is his lover.

programme.title: The Mongol Empire
programme.desc: Having consolidated his power over the Mongol tribes, Chinggis Khan has to decide how to save his unbeatable army; reviewing the geopolitical situation in inner Eurasia at the time; following Chinggis's forces on their campaigns outside of Mongolia.

programme.title: The Mongol Empire
programme.desc: Spotlighting three innovations introduced by Chinggis Khan to unify and modernize the Mongol state, from his reorganization of the Mongol society to taxation reforms and the creation of a new law code, the Great Yasa, which includes injunctions.

programme.title: Maya to Aztec: Ancient Mesoamerica Revealed
programme.desc: Surveying the geography, cultures and time span to be covered; discussing the organization of a study and its key concepts; learning and understanding important places, civilizations and events in Mesoamerica.

programme.title: Maya to Aztec: Ancient Mesoamerica Revealed
programme.desc: The Olmecs at the dawn of the Mesoamerican civilization; how the Olmecs represent one of only six cradles of early civilization in world history; how they were discovered; investigating three sites where they lived.

programme.title: Maya to Aztec: Ancient Mesoamerica Revealed
programme.sub-title: Olmec Art as the Mother Culture
programme.desc: Delving into Olmec art; searching for clues about who the Olmecs were and what preoccupied them; the mysteries of giant sculpted heads, jaguar carvings and full-bearded figures depicting men who some think were foreigners.

programme.title: Maya to Aztec: Ancient Mesoamerica Revealed
programme.desc: Investigating other cultures that thrived in Mesoamerica at the time of the Olmecs, such as the Zapotecs in the Oaxaca Valley; probing intriguing archeological evidence that raises the question of who influenced whom.

programme.title: Lost Worlds of South America
programme.sub-title: South America's Lost Cradle of Civilization
programme.desc: The evidence for South America as one of the true wellsprings of human civilization; the diversity of early South American cultures; what the cultures shared; innovations in agriculture, architecture, handicrafts, social organization and religion.

programme.title: Lost Worlds of South America
programme.desc: The first cities in the Americas, dating back to 3000 B.C.; investigating the means of subsistence of coastal and inland valley cities; evidence of trade in marine and agricultural products; learning about the sites of Kotosh, El Paraíso and Caral.

programme.title: Lost Worlds of South America
programme.desc: The earliest evidence of humans in the Americas; Monte Verde and its view into ancient life.

programme.title: Lost Worlds of South America
